provenance: Accounts were issued out of band (docs/alpha-testing-guide.md §2); the person-to-account mapping lives in the feedback survey's 'Your name' answer (docs/user-feedback-survey.md:19-22).

Accounts are provisioned in batches ahead of need -- five on 15 September 2026 and five more on 19 September, the second with pnpm testers:seed-sql (scripts/seed-testers.ts) -- so more accounts exist than are listed. Provisioned is not issued: an account gets an entry here only when it is handed to a person, and an account nobody holds is in no figure.
userId is the User.id UUID, which is also the PostHog distinct_id (docs/analytics/alpha-tracking-plan.md:51).

wallets are the G-addresses each tester signed with, read from SignedTransaction.signerAddress or the transaction_signed event. A tester signs with more than one, so this is a list. The per-tester walletAddresses field in the alpha-metrics snapshots carries the same addresses, so this list can be checked against a committed artefact rather than taken on trust.
No real name, username or email belongs in this file. The labels are pseudonyms and the published pages use them.
note: An entry appears when an account is issued, not when its session runs: a tester with no wallets and no events has been onboarded but has not yet worked through the guide, which was tester-3's state at the 18 September snapshot. tester-3 ran a session on 19 September, and its wallet was backfilled from the 26 September snapshot (alpha-metrics-2026-09-26.json, perTester). A tester who has run a session carries the wallets they signed with; those are backfilled from the snapshot, so an empty list beside a non-zero figure means this file is behind, not that the tester used none. plannedCohortSize is what the round targets; testers.length is what has been issued. Every alpha-tester figure is filtered on these UUIDs explicitly -- the PostHog cohort named 'Alpha testers' is role = USER, which since the 16 September cutover matches both ordinary paiflow.xyz visitors and sandbox sessions signing on the beta, and is deliberately not used. One of the issued accounts (tester-1) belongs to a member of the project, who ran the first session as a pilot of the protocol; the other two are external, and one of them (tester-2) ran their session on 18 September. About half of every alpha-tester figure in the 18 September snapshot is therefore the project's own work, which docs/instawards/metrics.md states alongside the numbers. One further provisioned account is used internally by the project; it is deliberately not listed, so nothing done under it is in any alpha-tester figure. The project member behind tester-1 also tests internally under a separate account and one of the wallets listed here was used by both, so their three wallets are three addresses belonging to one human, not three people.
